summary: Wojciech Marceli Gielecki was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who earned his Ph.D. at Jagiellonian University by 1901. He subsequently served as a librarian at Jagiellonian University from circa 1902 to 1939.

Wolfgang Adolf Theilkuhl was an Indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg (1919–1920) and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Munich (1918–1926). He served as a lecturer at King's College London from 1828 to 1833.

Sinologist Wolfgang Franke studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Hamburg. He held posts at Sichuan University (~1943–1945) and Peking University (~1945–1950) before succeeding Otto Franke in the sinology chair at Hamburg (~1950–1977).

Linguist Wolfgang Krause studied at Berlin and Göttingen under Schulze, Hermann, Wilamowitz-Moellendorff, and Pokorny, earning a Ph.D. in 1921. He served as professor of Indo-European linguistics at Königsberg (1929–1937) and Göttingen (1937–1963).

Wolfgang Lentz was a linguist and Iranian studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. at Göttingen in 1923, studying under Oldenberg, Sieg, Andreas, Lüders, and Müller. He worked at the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1924–1942) and the University of Hamburg (1950–1968).

Wolfgang Morgenroth was an Indologist and linguist who completed his PhD at the University of Jena under Richard Hauschild and habilitated at Greifswald. He held posts at Greifswald and served as professor of Indology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1972–1994).
Wolfgang Schlüter was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu from 1869 to 1874 under Leo Meyer. He later held an academic post at the University of Tartu from circa 1877 to 1914.

Wolfgang Schultz was a philosopher and historian who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Vienna around 1904. He served as administrator at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and held the philosophy chair at Munich in 1934.

Wolfgang Voigt was an Indologist who studied in Berlin and Marburg under Lüders, Breloer, Schaeder, Nobel, and Heiler. He directed the Royal Library of Berlin's Oriental Division (1949–1976) and founded the Verzeichnis der orientalischen Handschriften in Deutschland (1957–1982).

Wolfram Eberhard was a sinologist and historian who studied in Berlin under Ferdinand Lessing. He taught in China, served as professor of Sinology at Ankara University (1937–1948), and was professor of sociology at UC Berkeley (1948–1976).
Woncheol Yun, a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies, completed a PhD at Stony Brook University. He was attested in 2012 as a professor of religious studies at Seoul National University.

Woodford Wright Sherlock was an Indologist and linguist who received an M.A. from Trinity College Dublin in 1852. He worked as a lecturer in Hindustani at University College London (1884) and at the University of Cambridge (1883–1912).

Woosung Huh is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He was attested in 2012 as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University.
Wouter J. Hanegraaff is a religious studies scholar who studied at Utrecht University from circa 1982 to 1995. He held an academic post at the University of Amsterdam around 1999.
Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, both attested in 1999.

Władysław Kotwicz was a linguist and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at St. Petersburg University (1891–1895). He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1900–1923), Leningrad Orient Institute (1920–1923), and the University of Lviv (1924–1944).
Włodzimir Szajan was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Lviv from circa 1927 to 1936 under Stefan Bolesław Stasiak.
Xi Cao is a scholar active in the fields of computational studies and Tibetology, holding academic posts at both Minzu University of China and Tibet University.
Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from the University of Kelaniya and a PhD from the University of Hong Kong in 2016, with K. L. Dhammajoti serving as doctoral supervisor in 1995.

Xianlin Ji was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tsinghua and earned his PhD at Göttingen under Waldschmidt and Sieg. He held multiple leadership roles at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and was a professor and vice president at Peking University.
